pack_metadata.title: Export a first commercial goods order from India and complete payment realisation
pack_metadata.user_outcome: A first-time Indian exporter clears a commercial goods shipment, receives and reconciles the export proceeds through an authorised dealer bank, and obtains documentary realisation proof.
pack_metadata.central_scope: DGFT and Foreign Trade Policy, CBIC Customs and ICEGATE, Central GST treatment, RBI/FEMA export-proceeds rules, authorised dealer bank responsibilities, and operationally necessary private actors.
explicit_exclusions: Foreign-country import, product, labelling, sanctions, tax, and buyer-registration requirements; these are external dependencies to be evidenced for the destination.
A product-specific eight-digit ITC(HS) classification or export-policy conclusion without a complete product dossier and current Schedule II/notification check.

A case-specific SCOMET classification or authorization outcome without a complete technical/end-use/end-user dossier; defence, atomic-energy, wildlife, food, plant, animal, pharmaceutical, hazardous, precious-metal, and other specialist regimes remain outside the generic SCOMET branch.
State or municipal entity, premises, labour, factory, pollution, or trade licences except as an explicitly checked local dependency.
Automatic entitlement to RoDTEP, drawback, GST refund, export-promotion benefits, preferential origin, or any other incentive.
Private legal advice, buyer creditworthiness, freight pricing, insurance pricing, bank charges, Incoterm selection, and letter-of-credit document examination.
Postal, courier, SEZ, EOU, merchanting-trade, project-export, consignment-export, warehouse-abroad, and re-export variants.

qualifying_questions.question: What is the exporting entity type, PAN, active bank account, address, and current IEC status?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: IEC is ordinarily mandatory and its identity and bank data must match the exporter.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not file a commercial export shipping bill until an applicable IEC exemption is evidenced or an active IEC matching the exporter is obtained.

qualifying_questions.question: What exactly are the goods: composition, function, manufacturing process, model, end use, quantity, value, packaging, and any controlled or regulated characteristics?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: The eight-digit ITC(HS) code, export-policy status, product-regulator conditions, export duty, and documents are product-specific.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Unknown or ambiguous product facts stop policy classification, duty conclusions, licence conclusions, and customs filing.

qualifying_questions.question: Who is the buyer and consignee, what is the destination country, and who has evidenced the destination's import requirements?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Buyer risk and foreign legal requirements are not established by Indian public sources.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not dispatch until buyer identity, consignee, destination, import responsibility, and required foreign documents are evidenced by the buyer or a competent destination-country professional/authority.

qualifying_questions.question: What current Schedule II export-policy status and policy conditions apply to the exact eight-digit ITC(HS) code?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Free, restricted, prohibited, state-trading, SCOMET, and conditional goods follow materially different paths.
options: State trading or other conditional route
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Prohibited or unknown stops shipment; restricted or conditional status blocks shipping-bill filing until the exact authorisation and conditions are satisfied.

qualifying_questions.question: Is the exporter GST-registered, and will this order use LUT/bond without IGST or a currently notified payment-of-IGST route?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Exports are zero-rated, but refund mechanisms and eligibility are conditional and payment-of-IGST refund is no longer universally available.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not promise a refund or file a tax treatment on the shipping bill until registration status, route, export-duty status, and current eligibility are verified.

qualifying_questions.question: What payment method, currency, payer, due date, and document-routing arrangement are in the signed order?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Advance, open-account/collection, and letter-of-credit arrangements change risk, bank handling, document routing, and timing.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Unknown payment terms or a third-party/unsupported route requires AD-bank confirmation before dispatch; do not assume direct document dispatch is allowed.

qualifying_questions.question: Is an FTP authorisation, benefit, concession, or product-board registration being claimed that requires RCMC or an equivalent certificate?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: RCMC is conditional, not a blanket prerequisite for every ordinary free-goods shipment.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: If yes, identify the competent EPC/board and obtain current RCMC before the dependent authorisation or benefit claim; if no, do not add RCMC to the base path.

qualifying_questions.question: Will the exporter file through its own ICEGATE/RES setup, a licensed customs broker, or a Customs Service Centre?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: The submitting actor and credentials differ, but the exporter remains responsible for accurate declarations.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Confirm the submitter, authorisation, location, and tested filing channel before cargo handover.

qualifying_questions.question: Does the buyer or destination require a preferential or non-preferential certificate of origin, and on what authoritative basis?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Origin documentation depends on the destination, agreement, goods, and buyer claim; it is not universal.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not claim preference or procure a certificate until the applicable origin rule, issuing route, and supporting evidence are verified for the shipment.

qualifying_questions.question: Will any amount remain at buyer credit risk after shipment, and will the exporter seek ECGC or private credit insurance?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Credit insurance can mitigate specified commercial/political risks but is optional and policy-specific.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: If cover is desired, obtain a current written quote and policy terms before relying on protection; do not infer coverage from general guidance.

tasks.title: Establish the exporter identity and obtain or activate IEC
tasks.user_goal: Hold an active IEC that matches the exporting entity and bank account.
tasks.trigger: The entity intends to undertake its first commercial goods export and no applicable IEC exemption is evidenced.

fees_duties.label: New IEC application fee
fees_duties.applicability: New IEC application through the DGFT portal; re-check at payment before committing.

timelines.label: Bank validation
timelines.value: Near real time for many banks; may take up to 2 weeks for some banks
timelines.applicability: DGFT IEC application where NPCI bank validation remains pending; not a guaranteed issuance time.

steps: If a reusable-foundations IEC artifact already exists, verify its current active profile and CBIC transmission rather than creating a duplicate application.
Register or log in as Importer/Exporter on the DGFT portal.
Start Apply for IEC and enter entity, PAN, address, branch, bank, and activity details with the prescribed documents.
Sign with the supported DSC or Aadhaar e-Sign, pay through the portal, and retain the receipt.
Download the IEC certificate and confirm active status and CBIC transmission status before downstream registration.
tasks.tracking: DGFT My Dashboard / IEC profile and CBIC Transmission Status; retain the file/application and payment reference.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct failed PAN, address, bank, signature, duplicate-PAN, or document validation; use the portal application status and DGFT helpdesk/RA route shown for the case.
tasks.escalation: DGFT portal helpdesk, then the mapped Regional Authority where the application status or defect requires officer action.

state_local_dependency.description: The entity and premises may separately require state/local registrations; none is inferred as a nationwide export prerequisite.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Do not treat a draft, payment receipt, inactive IEC, or pending CBIC transmission as an active export identity.

tasks.title: Register the exporter on ICEGATE when using exporter-side customs services
tasks.user_goal: Obtain an ICEGATE ID and working authentication for the selected customs channel.
tasks.trigger: The exporter will use ICEGATE services directly or needs post-login bank-account/document-download functions.
steps: If approved ICEGATE credentials already exist, verify the current role and required post-login access rather than registering a duplicate user.
Use Register Now or Services > Registration and select the Importer/Exporter role.
Use identity/contact details aligned with PAN, GSTN where applicable, and DGFT; complete OTP and signature validation.
Submit electronically and retain the ICEGATE ID/registration confirmation.
Test login and the required post-login service before cargo is committed.
tasks.tracking: Use the ICEGATE registration enquiry/helpdesk route and registered email acknowledgements.
tasks.rejection_handling: Replace unclear or invalid documents, correct identity mismatches, and resubmit through the portal; do not email an ad-hoc registration request.
tasks.escalation: ICEGATE 24x7 helpdesk shown on the live portal, with the registration reference and screenshots excluding credentials.

state_local_dependency.description: No state/local dependency identified for ICEGATE registration itself.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Registration instructions are portal-version sensitive; verify the live form and never share DSC PINs, passwords, or OTPs.

tasks.title: Select the AD Category-I bank and align the export account
tasks.user_goal: Have the bank that will receive, report, and reconcile the export proceeds confirm the account and transaction route.
tasks.trigger: Before agreeing payment and document-routing terms or registering an AD code.

fees_duties.label: Bank remittance, collection, LC, document-handling, and conversion charges
fees_duties.applicability: Bank, currency, payment instrument, correspondent route, and customer-specific; obtain a written tariff/quote.

steps: Tell the AD bank this is a first goods export and provide IEC, entity, account, proposed buyer, currency, payer, payment method, and expected shipping location.
Obtain the branch AD code and written operational instructions for inward-remittance purpose, KYC, document routing, EDPMS matching, and exception handling.
Confirm that the same bank will handle the shipping documents when an advance is received through it.
tasks.tracking: Bank case/reference, relationship manager/compliance channel, and later IRM/EDPMS/export-bill references.
tasks.rejection_handling: Resolve KYC, account-name, purpose-code, payer, correspondent, or unsupported-instrument issues before accepting funds or dispatching documents.
tasks.escalation: AD bank trade-finance/forex operations and compliance head; RBI references are routed through the AD bank compliance head where required.

state_local_dependency.description: No state/local dependency identified for FEMA receipt through an AD bank.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Do not rely on a generic current account or payment-gateway promise as proof that the bank will report and reconcile the export receipt.

tasks.title: Validate buyer, order, payment, and document-routing terms
tasks.user_goal: Turn the commercial order into a signed, internally approved, bank-operable export transaction.
tasks.trigger: A foreign buyer proposes a first commercial goods order.

fees_duties.label: Credit-insurance premium or buyer limit
fees_duties.applicability: Only if a current ECGC/private-insurer offer is obtained for the named buyer, country, terms, and shipment.

steps: Verify buyer and consignee legal identity, contact, country, delivery address, and authority to order; retain the evidence supplied by private/foreign sources.

Sign a purchase order or sales contract stating goods, specifications, quantity, price, currency, delivery term, insurance/freight responsibility, payment instrument, payer, due date, and required documents.
Have the AD bank confirm any third-party payment, collection, direct-dispatch, LC, or advance arrangement it must handle; direct dispatch is not the default for a first exporter.
If using third-party payment, put the payer and supporting irrevocable-order/tripartite evidence into the contract and declaration workflow before receipt.
For post-shipment credit, decide whether to obtain a current buyer limit/insurance policy; do not infer cover from ECGC's general description.
tasks.tracking: Exporter order-risk checklist with links to buyer evidence, signed contract, bank confirmation, and any insurer quotation/policy.
tasks.rejection_handling: Renegotiate unsupported currency, payer, due date, direct-dispatch, documentary, or credit-risk terms; stop if buyer identity cannot be verified.
tasks.escalation: Exporter management/legal adviser, AD bank trade-finance team, and insurer/ECGC for policy-specific questions.

state_local_dependency.description: Commercial contracting has no identified uniform state/local export step; ordinary contract-law advice is private.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A signed order proves agreed private facts, not buyer solvency, foreign legality, bank acceptance, or insurance coverage.

tasks.title: Determine exact ITC(HS), export policy, conditions, and export-duty status
tasks.user_goal: Produce a shipment-specific classification and policy memo that can safely drive licensing, GST, and customs fields.
tasks.trigger: The complete product dossier and proposed shipment facts are available.

fees_duties.label: Export duty
fees_duties.applicability: Only after exact tariff classification, current tariff/notification, quantity/value, and exemption conditions are verified.

steps: Classify the goods to the exact eight-digit Indian tariff item from complete technical facts; record alternatives considered and why rejected.
Check the current DGFT Schedule II entry, policy conditions, general notes, country restrictions, and later notifications for that exact item.
Check other Central product regulators and Customs export-duty notifications that the goods' characteristics trigger.
Record the result as Free, Restricted, Prohibited, SCOMET/specialist, STE/conditional, or unresolved, with source locators and verification date.
tasks.tracking: Versioned classification/policy memo tied to the product model, composition, end use, and verification date.
tasks.rejection_handling: If facts or competing headings remain unresolved, obtain a qualified customs opinion and do not file; a Customs assessment/query may still require correction.
tasks.escalation: Qualified customs adviser and, where appropriate, the competent DGFT/Customs classification or policy-clarification route.

state_local_dependency.description: Product manufacture/storage may trigger state/local approvals, but no such approval is inferred from Central export policy.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The sources verify the classification framework, not this shipment's code, policy result, duty, exemption, or regulator status.

tasks.title: Close destination-country and buyer-document dependencies
tasks.user_goal: Obtain competent evidence that the named consignee can import the goods and that the required foreign-side documents are known.
tasks.trigger: The destination, consignee, and exact goods are known.
steps: Require the buyer/importer or a competent destination-country adviser/authority to identify import licences, product standards, labels, taxes, sanctions, origin documents, and clearance documents.
Map each foreign requirement to the responsible party and evidence artifact in the contract/document checklist.
Stop dispatch if the foreign-side conclusion is missing, contradictory, or outside the evidence supplied.
tasks.tracking: Shipment file containing foreign official/professional evidence and buyer acceptance of responsibility.
tasks.rejection_handling: Escalate to the destination importer, customs broker, regulator, or legal adviser; amend the contract or cancel shipment if clearance cannot be evidenced.
tasks.escalation: Named foreign importer and competent destination-country authority/professional; Indian authorities do not establish foreign import eligibility.

state_local_dependency.description: This is a foreign-country dependency, not an Indian state/local route.

tasks.fail_closed_note: No foreign-country requirement is invented or generalised in this pack.

tasks.title: Obtain the exact export authorisation or stop the shipment
tasks.user_goal: Hold a valid authorisation and satisfy its conditions before filing restricted goods.
tasks.trigger: The verified current policy result is Restricted non-SCOMET or otherwise requires DGFT permission.

fees_duties.label: Authorisation application fee
fees_duties.applicability: Depends on the exact authorisation/form and current fee schedule; verify in the live transaction before payment.

steps: Confirm that the route is non-SCOMET restricted goods and identify all item-specific policy conditions.
File the current online application; HBP identifies ANF 2N for non-SCOMET restricted export authorisation, with prescribed documents.
Track deficiency, committee/authority decision, validity, quantity/value, port, end-use, and pre/post-export conditions.
Do not ship prohibited goods; route SCOMET or other specialist regimes to separate verified research.
tasks.tracking: DGFT application/file number and the issued authorisation with condition checklist.
tasks.rejection_handling: Respond only through the official deficiency/appeal/review route stated for the application; do not reinterpret a rejection as permission.
tasks.escalation: DGFT Headquarters/Regional Authority identified in the application and a specialist export-control adviser for SCOMET or other excluded regimes.

state_local_dependency.description: The DGFT authorisation is Central; separate product/premises permissions may still apply.

tasks.fail_closed_note: This node does not prove that ANF 2N is correct for SCOMET, STE, prohibited, quota, or product-regulator cases.

tasks.title: Screen the current SCOMET list and obtain the applicable SCOMET authorisation
tasks.user_goal: Stop an uncontrolled export and hold a DGFT/competent-authority permission that matches the SCOMET item, end use and end user.
tasks.trigger: The current SCOMET list screen is positive or unresolved because technical parameters, software/technology, end use, end user or destination may be controlled.

fees_duties.label: SCOMET application fee
fees_duties.applicability: Live form and application-type specific; verify before payment.

steps: Reperform the screen against the current Appendix 3 SCOMET list using complete technical parameters, software/technology scope, end use, end user and destination; record the exact category or unresolved question.
For an ordinary SCOMET application, use the DGFT Export Management System route for ANF 2O(A); do not substitute the non-SCOMET ANF 2N route or assume GAICT applies.
Submit only the live form's prescribed item, end-use, end-user, purchase-order and supporting records; track deficiency and decision.
If approved, verify exporter, item/category, buyer/end user, destination, quantity/value, validity and every pre/post-export condition before quoting the authorisation in Customs.
tasks.tracking: DGFT application/file number, submitted application, deficiency responses and issued authorisation/condition checklist.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct only evidence-backed defects through the application route; a draft, fee receipt, deficiency reply or pending committee review is not permission.
tasks.escalation: DGFT SCOMET Cell/identified authority and a qualified export-control adviser; Category 0 or another competent-authority regime leaves this generic DGFT path.

state_local_dependency.description: This is the Central SCOMET control branch; premises/product permissions may separately apply.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The verified branch proves where and how to seek permission, not that the goods are outside SCOMET or that any application will be approved.

tasks.title: Obtain e-RCMC only when the dependent FTP route requires it
tasks.user_goal: Hold the competent council/board certificate needed for the identified authorisation, benefit, or concession.
tasks.trigger: An FTP authorisation other than the stated restricted-item exception, or a benefit/concession, requires RCMC/equivalent evidence.

fees_duties.label: Council/board membership and RCMC charge
fees_duties.applicability: Council, product, exporter category, period, and membership-specific; verify with the competent issuing body.

steps: Identify the competent EPC, commodity board, or development authority for the principal line of business.
Log in to DGFT and use Services > e-RCMC > Apply for e-RCMC with active IEC, updated profile, and linked signature.
Submit the issuer-specific documents and retain the issued certificate; do not add RCMC to a free-goods base path without a dependent requirement.
tasks.tracking: DGFT e-RCMC application status and the issuing body's certificate/reference.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct issuer selection, IEC/profile, signature, product-line, payment, or document defects with the named registering authority.
tasks.escalation: Competent EPC/commodity board and DGFT e-RCMC help route.

state_local_dependency.description: RCMC is a Central FTP/recognised-registering-authority dependency.

tasks.fail_closed_note: RCMC does not itself prove export-policy freedom, incentive eligibility, foreign compliance, or refund entitlement.

tasks.title: Select and document the GST export route
tasks.user_goal: Use a verified zero-rated-supply route without assuming refund entitlement.
tasks.trigger: The exporter's GST status, goods, and export-duty status are known.
steps: Confirm whether the exporter is registered and whether the goods are subject to export duty.
For a registered exporter, choose LUT/bond without IGST unless the exact class-of-persons/goods notification supporting payment-of-IGST refund has been verified.
Record invoice, return, shipping-bill, and refund implications; obtain tax advice if unregistered, exempt, or mixed facts apply.
tasks.tracking: Signed GST route memo tied to GSTIN, goods, tax period, export-duty conclusion, and current legal sources.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct the route before filing; do not cure an unsupported refund theory by changing only the shipping-bill declaration.
tasks.escalation: GST practitioner and jurisdictional GST officer/portal grievance route for a case-specific issue.

state_local_dependency.description: This pack covers Central zero-rating; state GST administration may process the taxpayer's case without creating a separate national route.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Zero-rating is not an automatic refund award; export duty, registration, returns, ITC, notification class, and realisation facts remain decisive.

tasks.title: File FORM GST RFD-11 LUT before exporting without IGST
tasks.user_goal: Hold an accepted LUT ARN for the applicable period before using the no-IGST route.
tasks.trigger: The GST-registered exporter selects the LUT route and is eligible to furnish LUT rather than bond.
steps: Log in to the GST common portal and open the LUT transaction for the relevant financial year.
Complete FORM GST RFD-11, sign, submit, and save the ARN acknowledgement.
Confirm the LUT remains applicable and was not rendered ineligible; if LUT is unavailable, obtain case-specific bond instructions.
tasks.tracking: GST portal LUT acknowledgement/ARN and status in the taxpayer account.
tasks.rejection_handling: If the portal or officer identifies ineligibility, do not use the LUT route; obtain current bond or corrective instructions.
tasks.escalation: GST portal grievance/helpdesk and jurisdictional tax officer.

state_local_dependency.description: No separate state/local step is asserted for the common-portal LUT submission.

tasks.fail_closed_note: An ARN acknowledges the LUT; it does not establish classification, export, ITC refund eligibility, or proceeds realisation.

tasks.title: Cure or obtain relief for failure to export goods within the LUT period
tasks.user_goal: Resolve a Rule 96A breach with evidenced export, permitted extension, or tax-and-interest payment before relying on the LUT route.
tasks.trigger: Goods invoiced for export under LUT are not exported within three months from the invoice date, or the exporter is approaching that limit without physical-export evidence.

fees_duties.label: Tax and applicable interest under Rule 96A
fees_duties.applicability: Compute only from the exact invoice, tax and payment dates or an evidenced Commissioner-allowed further period.

timelines.label: Goods export period under LUT
timelines.value: 3 months from invoice date, or a further period allowed by the Commissioner
timelines.applicability: Goods supplied for export without payment of IGST under Rule 96A.

timelines.label: Payment after unextended period expires
timelines.applicability: Tax due plus section 50(1) interest when the goods were not exported within the allowed period.

steps: Compare each export invoice date to authenticated LEO/EGM/physical-export evidence and the Rule 96A period.
Before assuming an extension, obtain a written Commissioner-allowed further period for the exact invoices; portal filing or a private explanation is not an extension.

If no valid further period applies and export did not occur, determine and pay the tax due with applicable interest within the prescribed cure period using the taxpayer's permitted GST payment/return route.
Retain the payment/reference or extension order and correct downstream refund assumptions.
tasks.tracking: Invoice-level LUT calendar, physical-export record, extension order or GST payment/return reference.
tasks.rejection_handling: Do not backdate export or extension evidence; resolve a portal/payment error through GST grievance and the jurisdictional officer.
tasks.escalation: Jurisdictional GST officer and qualified GST adviser for computation or extension authority.

state_local_dependency.description: Rule 96A is a Central GST-rule consequence handled through the competent GST administration.

tasks.fail_closed_note: An LUT ARN does not excuse missing physical export; without authenticated export or a valid further period, treat the tax/interest consequence as unresolved.

tasks.title: Register the AD-code bank account for the customs location
tasks.user_goal: Link the selected AD-bank branch/account to the ICEGATE customs location used for export.
tasks.trigger: The shipping location and designated AD-bank branch are known.
steps: Obtain the AD code/account proof from the selected AD bank.
In ICEGATE Bank Account management, add the Foreign Remittance Account for the exact customs location.
Enter bank, branch, AD code, account, location, document type/IRN and upload proof as required; verify and submit.
Retain success status and ensure the intended location/account appears before filing.
tasks.tracking: ICEGATE Bank Account page/status and submission evidence for the location.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct bank branch, AD code, account, customs location, IRN/document, or proof mismatch and re-verify.
tasks.escalation: AD-bank branch/trade operations for the code; ICEGATE helpdesk for portal/status issues.

state_local_dependency.description: Customs-location selection is Central customs operations, not a state/local licence.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A bank letter alone is not proof that the account is active for the exact ICEGATE customs location.

tasks.title: Book logistics and assemble the controlled shipment document pack
tasks.user_goal: Hand cargo to the correct private actors with consistent commercial, transport, regulatory, tax, and bank instructions.
tasks.trigger: Classification/policy, GST route, payment route, foreign requirements, and shipping location are closed.

fees_duties.label: Freight, insurance, customs-broker, terminal, handling, and carrier charges
fees_duties.applicability: Private quote, mode, route, cargo, Incoterm, port, and service-specific.

steps: Appoint the carrier/freight forwarder and, if used, licensed customs broker with written scope and authorisation.

Prepare consistent commercial invoice-cum-packing list, product description, quantity/UQC, value/currency, buyer/consignee, GST/LUT notation as advised, AD code, port, scheme, licence/NOC, and transport instructions.
Add only shipment-specific foreign, origin, insurance, inspection, and product documents that have been evidenced.
Run a four-way consistency check across contract, invoice/packing list, shipping-bill draft, and bank instructions.
tasks.tracking: Version-controlled document checklist and broker/forwarder handover acknowledgement.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct inconsistencies before filing or cargo cut-off; obtain revised buyer/carrier/bank acceptance where commercial facts change.
tasks.escalation: Customs adviser/broker for declaration data, AD bank for payment documents, and buyer/foreign adviser for destination documents.

state_local_dependency.description: Origin warehouse/factory, dangerous-goods handling, or local transport may trigger state/local permissions; none is inferred without cargo/location facts.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Private actor acceptance does not cure a wrong classification, missing authorisation, unsupported foreign requirement, or bank-routing mismatch.

tasks.title: Receive the export payment through the designated AD bank
tasks.user_goal: Create a bank-reported inward remittance that can be matched to the order and later shipping bill.
tasks.trigger: Payment is due under the signed order; for the demo this is full advance before shipment.

fees_duties.label: Bank and correspondent deductions
fees_duties.applicability: Transaction-specific and must be reconciled against remittance and invoice terms.

timelines.label: Shipment against ordinary export advance
timelines.value: Within 3 years from receipt of advance
timelines.applicability: Ordinary advance payment under RBI Master Direction C.2(1); more-than-three-year manufacturing arrangements have separate conditions.

steps: Give the buyer the designated account/remittance instructions and require the agreed payer, currency, invoice/order reference, and export purpose.
Obtain bank credit advice/IRM data and reconcile sender, amount, currency, purpose, deductions, and order.
If advance, schedule shipment within the applicable period and route shipment documents through the same AD bank.
tasks.tracking: AD-bank credit advice, IRM number/data, account credit, and EDPMS/export-advance reference where supplied.
tasks.rejection_handling: Do not self-characterise an unidentified, third-party, wrong-purpose, short, or wrong-currency receipt; ask the AD bank to correct/regularise it.
tasks.escalation: AD-bank forex/trade operations and compliance; buyer/remitting bank for missing or incorrect payment data.

state_local_dependency.description: No state/local dependency identified for receipt through the AD bank.

tasks.fail_closed_note: An account credit without correct bank reporting and transaction matching is not sufficient realisation proof.

tasks.title: File the electronic shipping bill and supporting documents
tasks.user_goal: Obtain a customs-acknowledged shipping bill with accurate declarations and document references.
tasks.trigger: All policy gates and cargo/document data are ready, and any required authorisation/RCMC/LUT is held.

fees_duties.label: Customs export duty or other levy
fees_duties.applicability: Exact goods, tariff item, quantity/value, notification, and exemption-specific; verify before filing/payment.

steps: Transmit the current ICES export declaration through the selected authorised channel and quote uploaded supporting-document references.
Check the acknowledgement and allotted shipping-bill number/date; compare every material field to the approved source pack.
Answer Customs queries with sourced corrections; amend before LEO where necessary and retain all message acknowledgements.
tasks.tracking: ICEGATE/ICES shipping-bill acknowledgement, query/reply messages, and signed shipping-bill copy.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the query-reply/amendment message route; do not create a replacement declaration without resolving duplicate or data-consistency risk.
tasks.escalation: Selected customs broker/Service Centre, ICEGATE helpdesk for message errors, and the jurisdictional Customs officer for assessment issues.

state_local_dependency.description: The electronic shipping bill is a Central Customs transaction.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A file upload or job number is not Customs acceptance; require the shipping-bill acknowledgement/number and resolve queries.

tasks.title: Resolve a Shipping Bill negative acknowledgement or Customs query
tasks.user_goal: Reach a positive acknowledgement and closed query state without duplicating or silently changing the declaration.
tasks.trigger: ICEGATE/ICES returns CHCAE02_NAK, CHCAE03, another filing defect, or the document-status enquiry does not show an accepted Shipping Bill.
steps: Preserve the rejected message/negative acknowledgement or Customs query and identify the exact field/document defect.
Correct the controlled source data first, then retransmit or use the supported Query Reply message/webform through the authorised filing channel.
Check ICEGATE Shipping Bill current status and retain the positive acknowledgement, query reply and any accepted amendment.
Do not present cargo for LEO while a negative acknowledgement or material query remains unresolved.
tasks.tracking: CHCAE02_ACK/NAK, CHCAE03/CACHE04, Shipping Bill current status and accepted amendment references.
tasks.rejection_handling: Escalate a technical transmission defect to ICEGATE helpdesk and an assessment/document defect to the proper Customs officer; do not create an unlinked duplicate Shipping Bill.
tasks.escalation: Customs broker/Service Centre, ICEGATE helpdesk and jurisdictional Customs officer with message and document references.

state_local_dependency.description: Shipping Bill message remediation is a Central Customs workflow.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Only a positive acknowledgement/current accepted status and closed material query allows the Customs path to continue.

tasks.title: Present cargo, complete risk-based Customs processing, and obtain LEO
tasks.user_goal: Receive Let Export Order for the declared cargo before export loading.
tasks.trigger: Cargo arrives at the customs location and is registered against the shipping bill.
steps: Complete goods registration/carting and present cargo/documents through the custodian/broker route.
Follow the ICES risk-management outcome for assessment, query, examination, sampling, or facilitation; do not assume examination or waiver.
Resolve recorded discrepancies and obtain LEO from the proper officer.
Download and retain the signed LEO copy/gate pass through ICEGATE.
tasks.tracking: ICES/ICEGATE status, examination/query records, signed LEO and gate pass.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct or amend declaration/document/cargo discrepancies under Customs instructions; a hold, query, or examination is not clearance.
tasks.escalation: Jurisdictional Customs assessment/examination officer and ICEGATE helpdesk for download/status issues.

state_local_dependency.description: LEO is Central Customs clearance; custodian operations are private/regulated dependencies.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Do not treat filing, goods registration, assessment, or examination completion as LEO.

tasks.title: Load and export the goods and secure transport/EGM evidence
tasks.user_goal: Prove physical export after LEO and obtain the carrier transport document and Customs manifestation status.
tasks.trigger: LEO has been issued and the carrier accepts the cargo for loading.
steps: Release cargo for loading only after LEO and preserve the final airway bill/bill of lading or other applicable transport receipt.
Require the carrier/shipping line/agent to file the shipping-bill-wise EGM electronically.
Track EGM and physical-export confirmation; resolve short shipment, shut-out, mismatch, or manifest error before relying on export completion.
tasks.tracking: Carrier departure/transport document plus ICEGATE/Customs EGM or shipping-bill status.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use carrier and Customs correction procedures for shut-out, short shipment, wrong transport reference, or EGM errors; update bank/GST records where affected.
tasks.escalation: Carrier/agent and jurisdictional Customs export/manifest section; ICEGATE helpdesk for status display problems.

state_local_dependency.description: EGM is Central Customs reporting by the carrier; port/custodian operations remain private dependencies.

tasks.fail_closed_note: LEO alone does not prove that the goods left India; require transport and EGM/physical-export evidence.

tasks.title: Lodge shipping documents with the AD bank
tasks.user_goal: Give the designated AD bank the documents needed to handle, report, and match the export bill/advance.
tasks.trigger: The shipment has exported and final shipping documents are available.

timelines.label: Lodgement of prescribed export documents with AD bank
timelines.value: Within 21 days from date of export
timelines.applicability: RBI B.1/B.2; EDI shipping-bill EC-copy submission is not required where not printed and shipping-bill data is integrated with EDPMS, but the bank's remaining document requirements still apply.

steps: Submit the final invoice, transport document, shipping-bill/LEO details, order/payment terms, and bank-requested documents to the named AD bank within the applicable period; where EDI data removes the EC-copy printout, still satisfy the bank's remaining document requirements.
For advance, direct the bank to match the IRM/advance to the shipping bill and invoice through the same AD bank.

For collection or LC, route negotiable/shipping documents exactly as the contract, LC and AD-bank instructions require; use an HAWB/FCR only within the RBI conditions and not as a universal substitute for the transport document.
Obtain the bank's export-bill/reference and resolve discrepancies rather than assuming ICEGATE transmission completed bank handling.
tasks.tracking: AD-bank export-bill/document-lodgement reference and EDPMS/IRM matching status.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct missing documents, values, dates, AD code, purpose, payer, or shipping-bill mismatch; the AD may handle late submission when satisfied with reasons, but delay is not a default route.
tasks.escalation: AD-bank trade-finance operations and compliance, with shipping-bill/IRM/export-bill references.

state_local_dependency.description: No state/local dependency identified for AD-bank document handling.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Do not treat email delivery or an account credit as successful EDPMS/export-bill matching; obtain a bank reference/status.

tasks.title: Reconcile invoice, shipping bill, remittance, and EDPMS realisation
tasks.user_goal: Show that the full required export value is realised/repatriated and correctly matched by the AD bank.
tasks.trigger: The export documents and inward remittance exist; for credit terms, when payment arrives or becomes due.

timelines.label: Realisation and repatriation of ordinary goods export proceeds
timelines.applicability: Ordinary exports under RBI A.2(i); warehouse-abroad and specified special cases differ.

steps: Match invoice currency/value, FOB value, shipping-bill number/date/port/AD code, payer, IRM amount/date/purpose, bank deductions, and any approved adjustment.
Ask the AD bank to update EDPMS on an as-realised basis and close/match the relevant export entry.
For a declared third-party payer, verify the irrevocable order/tripartite or permitted substitute evidence, banking-channel receipt, EDF declaration and AD-bank bona-fides review before matching.
For an EDPMS entry of INR 10 lakh equivalent or less, ask the AD bank whether the current exporter-declaration reconciliation procedure applies; do not self-close the entry.
Record any short, excess, third-party, deduction, currency, or reference variance and obtain the bank-approved treatment before declaring completion.
tasks.tracking: Reconciliation statement plus AD-bank confirmation/EDPMS status and IRM/export-bill references.
tasks.rejection_handling: Resolve unmatched entries with the AD bank; if the due date or FEMA period is at risk, trigger non-realisation remediation before expiry.
tasks.escalation: AD-bank trade operations/compliance; unresolved regulatory cases through the AD bank to the RBI Regional Office.

state_local_dependency.description: FEMA/EDPMS reconciliation is Central-regulator and AD-bank handling.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Full account credit is not enough if the export entry remains unmatched or an unapproved deduction/value difference exists.

tasks.title: Resolve missing, mismatched, or stale Shipping Bill/EDPMS transmission and matching data
tasks.user_goal: Obtain a clean Customs-to-EDPMS status and AD-bank matching record before eBRC completion.
tasks.trigger: The Shipping Bill is absent from RBI-EDPMS/DGFT, shows a transmission error, or cannot be matched to the bank-reported remittance/export bill.
steps: Use ICEGATE Shipping Bill in RBI-EDPMS enquiry to check transmission date/status against location, Shipping Bill number and date.

For an ICEGATE-side EDPMS status defect, raise the authenticated Rectification of SB in RBI-EDPMS query and retain the reference; for bank-side IRM/export-bill data, route correction through the AD bank.
If the Shipping Bill is not visible at DGFT, use the authenticated DGFT Retransmission Facility (SB) with Shipping Bill date/number, port code and IEC, then track DGFT Retransmission Status.
Reperform the invoice/Shipping Bill/IRM/export-bill match and continue only after the relevant system and AD-bank statuses agree.
tasks.tracking: ICEGATE EDPMS enquiry/rectification reference, DGFT retransmission status, AD-bank correction reference and final matched EDPMS status.
tasks.rejection_handling: Separate Customs transmission, DGFT visibility and bank-reporting defects; send each to the competent channel rather than repeatedly altering source identifiers.
tasks.escalation: ICEGATE helpdesk for Customs transmission/status, AD-bank trade operations/compliance for IRM/EDPMS matching, and DGFT helpdesk for post-retransmission visibility.

state_local_dependency.description: This is Central Customs/RBI/DGFT system reconciliation plus AD-bank handling.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A submitted rectification/retransmission request is not resolution; require final system visibility and AD-bank match.

tasks.title: Generate, review, and retain eBRC
tasks.user_goal: Obtain DGFT documentary proof linking the bank-reported inward remittance to the goods shipping bill.
tasks.trigger: The bank IRM is visible and the goods shipping bill/invoice date exists; an advance cannot be certificated before that date.
steps: Log in with the IEC-linked DGFT profile and open Services > eBRC > Generate e-BRC.
Select goods, enter the IRM amount/number, and verify bank/purpose/currency/remittance data populated from the bank message.
Enter AD code, GST selection/details where applicable, branch, shipping-bill number/date/port/currency/value and permitted deductions; preview carefully.
Accept the declaration, sign/submit, retain the eBRC number and download it from Bills Repository; respond through Respond to Bank/Agency if RMS marks it Under Review.
tasks.tracking: DGFT My Dashboard > Bills Repository and eBRC number/status; retain IRM utilisation and response logs.
tasks.rejection_handling: If IRM is absent/wrong, ask the AD bank to correct/report it; if shipping-bill data or deductions mismatch, correct the supported fields; if Under Review, submit remarks/attachments through the official response route.
tasks.escalation: AD bank for IRM/EDPMS data, DGFT eBRC helpdesk for portal issues, and the responding bank/agency for an RMS review.

state_local_dependency.description: eBRC is a Central DGFT/bank-data process.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A generated eBRC that is Under Review, contains mismatched shipment/remittance data, or uses an unsupported deduction is not final clean proof.

tasks.title: Correct, cancel, or respond to an unusable eBRC
tasks.user_goal: Restore a clean DGFT realisation proof without cancelling an already-utilised or bank-generated certificate outside the permitted route.
tasks.trigger: The eBRC is Under Review, has wrong shipment/remittance/deduction data, cannot be used, or must be cancelled before benefit use.
steps: Check Bills Repository and the IRM Utilisation Report to identify review status, utilised value and the exact data conflict.
For Under Review, use Services > eBRC > Respond to Bank/Agency, supply evidence-backed remarks/attachment and retain Response Submitted; the IRM remains unusable while under review.
If an exporter-generated eBRC is wrong and has not been used for benefits, refunds, remission or credits, initiate cancellation from Bills Repository, provide mandatory remarks/declaration and sign.
Do not cancel a bank-generated eBRC or an already-utilised exporter-generated eBRC through this route; obtain the competent DGFT/bank correction path and retain the final clean certificate/status.
tasks.tracking: Bills Repository status, IRM Utilisation Report, response/cancellation reference and replacement/final eBRC.
tasks.rejection_handling: If the defect originates in IRM/EDPMS, return to the AD-bank/EDPMS remediation branch; portal re-entry cannot cure bank source data.
tasks.escalation: AD bank for source data, DGFT eBRC helpdesk for portal/cancellation issues, and the reviewing bank/agency for RMS disposition.

state_local_dependency.description: eBRC remediation is a Central DGFT/bank-data workflow.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Response Submitted, Initiate Cancel, or a new draft is not documentary completion; require a final clean and usable eBRC status.

tasks.title: Claim accumulated-ITC refund only after shipment-specific eligibility review
tasks.user_goal: Submit an eligible GST RFD-01 claim using consistent return, shipping-bill, EGM, and invoice data.
tasks.trigger: The exporter seeks refund of unutilised ITC after a LUT export and has verified legal and factual eligibility.
steps: Verify registration, LUT, returns, ITC, export-duty exclusion, invoice/shipping-bill/EGM consistency, and current section 54/rule 89 eligibility for the tax period.
File FORM GST RFD-01 under the correct category with turnover, Statement 3/3A data, shipping-bill and EGM details, and required declarations/documents.
Save the ARN, track officer processing, and answer deficiency/query through the portal; do not treat system calculation as entitlement.
tasks.tracking: GST portal Track Application Status using ARN, followed by the sanction/rejection/payment order where issued.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the deficiency/refiling or response route supported by the portal/order; correct source returns/invoice data where legally permitted before re-claiming.
tasks.escalation: Jurisdictional refund officer, GST portal grievance route, and tax adviser for appeal or substantive eligibility issues.

state_local_dependency.description: The common GST portal is national; the competent tax administration may be Central or State depending on registration.

tasks.fail_closed_note: This task is excluded from the demo happy path because exact ITC/refund entitlement was not established.

tasks.title: Respond to GST refund deficiency, proposed rejection, or bank-validation failure
tasks.user_goal: Obtain a procedurally valid corrected application or final disposition without treating a portal calculation or deficiency reply as entitlement.
tasks.trigger: The portal/officer issues RFD-03, RFD-08, a refund-status/bank-validation failure, or another correction request.

timelines.label: Reply to RFD-08
timelines.applicability: Reply in FORM GST RFD-09 to a proposed whole/part refund rejection under the official refund rules.

steps: Read the electronic order/notice and separate an RFD-03 completeness deficiency from an RFD-08 proposed substantive rejection or a PFMS/bank-account validation failure.
For RFD-03, rectify the identified deficiency and file the corrected claim as a fresh refund application; preserve the re-credit/ledger treatment and new ARN.
For RFD-08, file RFD-09 with evidence within the prescribed period and track the RFD-06 decision; do not bypass the hearing/appeal route with a duplicate claim.
For bank-validation failure, correct the registered bank-account data through the permitted registration amendment/update function, then use the ARN-linked update and track PFMS/GST status.
tasks.tracking: RFD-03/RFD-08/RFD-09, fresh ARN, RFD-06/RFD-05, bank-validation status and ledger re-credit reference as applicable.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the statutory reply, fresh-application, hearing or appeal route that matches the issued form; correct source returns only through legally permitted amendments.
tasks.escalation: Jurisdictional refund officer, GST portal grievance/PFMS status route and qualified GST adviser for substantive dispute or appeal.

state_local_dependency.description: The common GST procedure is national; the competent tax officer may be Central or State for the registration.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A fresh ARN, response submission or status update is not refund entitlement or payment; require the applicable final order and credited amount.

tasks.title: Handle overdue, short, or non-realised export proceeds
tasks.user_goal: Act before the regulatory deadline and obtain an AD-bank/RBI-approved extension, correction, recovery, or write-off treatment.
tasks.trigger: Payment is overdue, short, disputed, unmatched, or unlikely to be realised within the applicable FEMA period.

timelines.label: AD-bank extension increment
timelines.value: Up to 6 months at a time
timelines.applicability: Only when RBI C.20 conditions are satisfied; other cases require RBI Regional Office approval.

timelines.label: Ordinary realisation period
timelines.applicability: Use the actual applicable FEMA period and any valid extension for the shipment.

steps: Monitor the contractual due date and FEMA deadline; document recovery efforts and the reason for delay.
Before expiry, ask the handling AD bank for an extension where eligible or for routing to the RBI Regional Office; ensure EDPMS reporting.
For unrecoverable amounts, use only the current self/AD write-off conditions with documentary evidence; surrender proportionate incentives where required.
If a GST export refund was received, address the statutory deposit/interest consequence for non-realisation; do not treat a rupee insurance settlement as foreign-exchange realisation.
tasks.tracking: AD-bank/RBI extension, recovery, EDPMS closure/write-off, incentive surrender, GST deposit/re-refund, and insurer claim references as applicable.
tasks.rejection_handling: If AD-bank delegation conditions are not met, route the request through the AD bank to RBI; continue recovery and do not backdate or self-invent an extension/write-off.
tasks.escalation: AD-bank compliance head, RBI Regional Office through the AD bank, DGFT for incentive surrender, GST officer for refund consequences, and insurer for a covered claim.

state_local_dependency.description: The core non-realisation route is FEMA/DGFT/GST and AD-bank handling.

tasks.fail_closed_note: An insurer payment, collection effort, buyer promise, or internal write-off does not by itself close EDPMS or satisfy FEMA/GST/FTP consequences.

dependency_edges.condition: Active IEC exists and exporter-side ICEGATE services are needed.
Exporter identity can be onboarded by the AD bank.
Payment and document terms need bank-operable confirmation.
Exporter and shipment product dossier are available.
Buyer, consignee and destination are fixed.
Exact goods are known for the external check.
Verified policy status requires non-SCOMET restricted export authorisation; prohibited/SCOMET/STE cases leave this route.
The current SCOMET screen is positive or unresolved; prohibited or other competent-authority regimes do not enter an ordinary ANF 2O(A) path.
An identified FTP authorisation, benefit or concession requires RCMC/equivalent.
Classification and export-duty status inform GST route/refund eligibility.
Registered exporter chooses and qualifies for LUT rather than bond/payment route.
Goods are not physically exported within the Rule 96A period or authenticated export evidence is missing.
Post-login account management is used.
Bank supplies designated AD-code/account evidence.
Commercial and payment terms are approved.
Classification/policy memo is complete.
GST route and any LUT are known.
Customs location and bank account link are active.
Unresolved foreign requirements block final document pack and dispatch.
Payment becomes due under the signed order.
Designated AD receipt route is confirmed.
Controlled document pack is final.
Applies only where authorisation is required; valid conditions must be satisfied before filing.
Applies when SCOMET is triggered; exact competent permission and conditions must be satisfied before filing.
Only when the specific authorisation requires RCMC; the restricted-item exception in FTP must be applied exactly.
Customs acknowledged the shipping bill and cargo is presented.
A negative acknowledgement, query, filing defect or non-accepted current status exists.
When remediation is triggered, positive acknowledgement/current accepted status and closed material query are required before LEO processing continues.
LEO issued before loading/export.
Final shipment and transport documents are available.
Bank-reported receipt exists.
AD bank has shipping documents/export-bill data.
Shipping Bill transmission, DGFT visibility or bank EDPMS/IRM matching remains missing or inconsistent.
IRM and shipment data can be linked in DGFT.
When system remediation is triggered, final Customs/DGFT visibility and AD-bank match are required before clean eBRC completion.
The certificate is Under Review, incorrect, unusable, or eligible for cancellation before benefit use.
Exporter separately establishes accumulated-ITC refund eligibility.
Refund claim is for exports without payment of IGST under LUT.
RFD-03, RFD-08, bank-validation failure or another formal correction/rejection status is issued.
Payment is overdue, short, disputed, unmatched, or at risk.
Non-realisation consequences must be resolved for a received/proposed export refund.

authorities_actors.name: Indian exporter
authorities_actors.role: Owns declarations, commercial facts, documents, proceeds realisation, and retention of proof.
authorities_actors.channel: DGFT/GST/ICEGATE portals, AD bank, and private actors

authorities_actors.name: Directorate General of Foreign Trade
authorities_actors.role: Administers IEC, Foreign Trade Policy, export authorisations, e-RCMC platform, and eBRC platform.

authorities_actors.name: DGFT Regional Authority or Headquarters
authorities_actors.role: Processes jurisdictional or headquarters applications and deficiencies according to the selected DGFT transaction.

authorities_actors.name: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs / jurisdictional Customs
authorities_actors.role: Administers shipping-bill assessment, risk processing, examination, LEO, and physical-export records.

authorities_actors.name: ICEGATE / Indian Customs National Trade Portal
authorities_actors.role: Customs registration, electronic messages, bank-account management, acknowledgements, downloads, and status services.

authorities_actors.name: GST common portal and competent GST administration
authorities_actors.role: Receives LUT and refund transactions and administers zero-rated-supply consequences.

authorities_actors.name: Reserve Bank of India
authorities_actors.role: Issues FEMA export-proceeds directions and handles non-delegated cases through Regional Offices.
authorities_actors.channel: RBI directions; references ordinarily routed through AD-bank compliance head

authorities_actors.name: Authorised Dealer Category-I bank
authorities_actors.role: Receives export proceeds, reports IRM/EDPMS data, handles shipping documents, follows overdue bills, and processes delegated extension/write-off cases.

authorities_actors.name: Competent Export Promotion Council, commodity board, or recognised registering authority
authorities_actors.role: Issues RCMC/equivalent for its recognised product/sector scope when required.

authorities_actors.name: Licensed customs broker or Customs Service Centre
authorities_actors.role: Operationally files or assists with Customs declarations under authority; optional if exporter has a supported direct route.

authorities_actors.name: Carrier, shipping line, airline, freight forwarder, agent, and custodian as applicable
authorities_actors.role: Books, receives, transports, manifests, and evidences physical export; shipping line/agent files EGM.
authorities_actors.channel: Private systems and Customs manifest interface

authorities_actors.name: Foreign buyer, payer, and consignee
authorities_actors.role: Supplies private identity/order facts, pays under the contract, and assigns foreign import responsibility.

authorities_actors.name: Foreign importer, authority, or competent destination-country professional
authorities_actors.role: Supplies authoritative foreign import, product, origin, tax, sanctions, and clearance requirements outside this pack.

authorities_actors.name: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Limited or other regulated export-credit insurer
authorities_actors.role: May quote and issue policy-specific commercial/political risk cover; cover is never inferred.

authorities_actors.name: Qualified tax/customs adviser
authorities_actors.role: Provides case-specific classification, duty, GST, refund, and specialist-regime analysis where public sources do not resolve the facts.
authorities_actors.channel: Written opinion tied to source evidence

portal_journeys.name: DGFT new IEC application
portal_journeys.authentication: DGFT Importer/Exporter account; registered email/mobile; supported DSC or Aadhaar e-Sign.
portal_journeys.navigation: Login/Register as Importer/Exporter > dashboard Apply for IEC > Start Fresh Application.
inputs_uploads: active bank account and cancelled cheque/bank certificate
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Payment receipt, IEC certificate, and CBIC Transmission Status.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: My Dashboard / My IEC / IEC profile and submitted-request tracking.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Correct NPCI/PAN/document/signature failure; use DGFT helpdesk and mapped RA for officer-dependent cases.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Authenticated transaction; live fields and fee must be rechecked at submission.

portal_journeys.name: ICEGATE Importer/Exporter registration
portal_journeys.authentication: Pre-registration OTP and identity validation; IEC-holder contact details must align with DGFT/GSTN; DSC/Aadhaar requirements apply per live form.
portal_journeys.navigation: Register Now or Services > Registration > Registration on ICEGATE; choose Importer/Exporter role and complete the electronic form.
inputs_uploads: colour JPG/PDF uploads within live limits
portal_journeys.submission_proof: ICEGATE ID/registration confirmation and registered-email acknowledgement.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: Registration enquiry/helpdesk route using the application/reference number.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Correct unclear documents or identity/contact mismatches; contact ICEGATE helpdesk with reference.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Authenticated form; the public ICEGATE registration index was live, but role fields remain portal-version sensitive.

portal_journeys.name: DGFT non-SCOMET restricted export authorisation
portal_journeys.authentication: IEC-linked DGFT account and supported signature.
portal_journeys.navigation: Online DGFT export-management transaction for non-SCOMET restricted export authorisation; HBP paragraph 2.68 identifies ANF 2N.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: DGFT file/application number and, if approved, signed export authorisation with conditions.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Respond to deficiency or use the stated review/appeal route; specialist SCOMET/STE/prohibited cases leave this journey.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Authenticated; the exact live menu label, fee, and item-specific document list must be confirmed in the transaction.

portal_journeys.name: DGFT Export Authorisation of SCOMET Items
portal_journeys.authentication: IEC-linked DGFT account and supported DSC/e-Sign.
portal_journeys.navigation: Services > Export Management System > Export of Restricted Items > Export Authorisation of SCOMET Items, Software/Technology > ANF 2O(A) Apply for New Authorisation.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: DGFT application/file number and, if approved, SCOMET authorisation with conditions.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: DGFT draft/submitted applications and authorisation status.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Respond to the stated deficiency; GAICT uses ANF 2O(B), while Category 0/other competent-authority cases leave this generic journey.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Authenticated and case-specific; live documents, fee, committee/authority and post-reporting conditions control.

portal_journeys.name: DGFT e-RCMC application
portal_journeys.authentication: Active IEC, updated IEC profile, and linked DSC or Aadhaar e-Sign.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: e-RCMC application reference and issued certificate.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Correct issuer/product/profile/document defects with the selected registering authority.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Authenticated; issuer-specific charges and documents are not uniform.

portal_journeys.name: GST FORM GST RFD-11 LUT
portal_journeys.authentication: GST taxpayer login and authorised signatory.
portal_journeys.navigation: GST common portal LUT transaction for furnishing FORM GST RFD-11 for the relevant financial year.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Online acknowledgement bearing ARN; circular states LUT is deemed accepted on ARN generation.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: GST taxpayer account, submitted LUT acknowledgement and invoice-level physical-export/payment records.
portal_journeys.exception_route: If ineligible for LUT, obtain current bond/corrective instructions; if Rule 96A goods-export timing fails, retain a Commissioner-allowed further period or pay the exact tax/interest through the permitted GST route.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Authenticated; current menu wording, eligibility, extension authority and payment mechanics must be checked live.

portal_journeys.name: ICEGATE Foreign Remittance Account / AD code registration
portal_journeys.authentication: ICEGATE registered user; signature/role requirements per live account-management module.
portal_journeys.navigation: Post login > Bank Account > Foreign Remittance Account (Authorised Dealer Code) > Add New Bank Account.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Verified/success status in Bank Account management for the selected location.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Modify or re-add after correcting bank/location/document data; use bank and ICEGATE helpdesk.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Post-login functionality; advisory page was current on 25 August 2026 and links operational material.

portal_journeys.name: ICES electronic export declaration / shipping-bill messages
portal_journeys.authentication: Authorised exporter/customs-broker/RES or Service Centre route with current signing and message setup.
portal_journeys.navigation: Transmit CACHE01 Shipping Bill; require CHCAE02_ACK, not CHCAE02_NAK; answer CHCAE03 through CACHE04 Query Reply or the supported post-login webform.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: CHCAE02_ACK, allotted Shipping Bill number/date, closed material query and later signed copy.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: Pre-login Services > Quick Information or post-login Services > Enquiries > Shipping Bill; inspect current and EGM status plus acknowledgements.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Preserve CHCAE02_NAK/CHCAE03; correct source data and use CACHE04/supported Query Reply; ICEGATE helpdesk handles transmission/display errors and Customs handles assessment defects.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: The public message list verifies IDs but not a universal browser filing form; use a current authorised channel and authenticated status for the shipment.

portal_journeys.name: ICEGATE LEO signed-copy download
portal_journeys.authentication: ICEGATE login with access to the export job.
portal_journeys.navigation: Download e-Copy widget > Let Export Order (LEO) > search by date or job number.
inputs_uploads: date range or location code/job number/job date
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Downloaded acknowledgement and signed LEO copy; gate-pass download where applicable.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Confirm job/location/date and LEO issuance; use ICEGATE helpdesk if an issued record is unavailable.

portal_journeys.name: ICEGATE Shipping Bill in RBI-EDPMS enquiry and rectification
portal_journeys.authentication: Public status enquiry; ICEGATE login for rectification and foreign-exchange realisation details.
portal_journeys.navigation: Services > Enquiries/Public Enquiries > Shipping Bill in RBI-EDPMS; post login use Rectification of SB in RBI-EDPMS for an identified status defect.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Displayed transmission/status and, when needed, rectification query reference plus corrected final status.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: Repeat the Shipping Bill in RBI-EDPMS enquiry and retain the before/after status with AD-bank reference.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Use ICEGATE rectification only for Customs-side status; use AD bank for IRM/export-bill reporting and matching.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Public status does not authenticate payment realisation; rectification and realised-amount detail require login and final system confirmation.

portal_journeys.name: ICEGATE retransmission of Shipping Bill to DGFT
portal_journeys.authentication: ICEGATE login for the IEC/exporter role.
portal_journeys.navigation: Dashboard > Services > ICEGATE Enquiry Service > DGFT Enquiry > DGFT Retransmission Facility (SB); track in DGFT Retransmission Status Enquiry.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Retransmission request and final DGFT Retransmission Status.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: DGFT Retransmission Status Enquiry using the shipment identifiers.
portal_journeys.exception_route: If still absent after final status, use ICEGATE helpdesk with request/status and DGFT helpdesk with the shipment reference.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: The route corrects DGFT visibility only; it does not prove Customs clearance, payment, EDPMS matching or benefit eligibility.

portal_journeys.name: GST refund of unutilised ITC for exports without payment of tax
portal_journeys.authentication: GST taxpayer login with required returns filed and authorised signatory.
portal_journeys.navigation: Refund application > FORM GST RFD-01 > refund of unutilised ITC on account of exports without payment of tax.
portal_journeys.submission_proof: ARN, followed by RFD-02/RFD-03, RFD-08/RFD-09, RFD-06/RFD-05 and credited payment/status as applicable.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: Services > Track Application Status > Refund using ARN; also track PFMS/bank-account validation when shown.
portal_journeys.exception_route: RFD-03 requires rectification and a fresh application; RFD-08 is answered by RFD-09 within 15 days; correct bank data through the permitted registration/ARN-linked update route.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Portal/remediation procedure is verified; shipment-specific entitlement, amount and appeal outcome are not.

portal_journeys.name: DGFT Generate and remediate eBRC from IRM
portal_journeys.authentication: DGFT Importer/Exporter account linked to IEC; supported DSC/e-Sign for declaration/submission/cancellation.
portal_journeys.navigation: Services > eBRC > Generate e-BRC; My Dashboard > Bills Repository; IRM Utilisation Report; Under Review via Respond to Bank/Agency; eligible cancellation via Repository > eBRC > Initiate Cancel.
inputs_uploads: GST-benefit selection and GSTIN/invoice data where applicable
portal_journeys.submission_proof: eBRC number and downloadable clean certificate/status, or final remediation/cancellation status where applicable.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: Bills Repository, IRM Utilisation Report, response status and cancellation status.
portal_journeys.exception_route: Under Review uses Respond to Bank/Agency; only an unused exporter-generated eBRC is eligible for portal cancellation; bank-generated or utilised records require the competent bank/DGFT correction path.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Advance IRM cannot generate eBRC before Shipping Bill/invoice date; Under Review IRM is unusable and cancellation is restricted.

required_inputs.name: Entity identity, PAN, address, constitution and authorised-person evidence
required_inputs.format_validity: Use the live portal/bank-prescribed documents; names and identifiers must match.

required_inputs.name: Active bank account proof
required_inputs.format_validity: Cancelled cheque or bank certificate for IEC as listed in current DGFT manual; bank-specific KYC separately applies.

required_inputs.name: Supported DSC or Aadhaar e-Sign capability
required_inputs.when_required: DGFT, ICEGATE and GST submissions as the live transaction requires
required_inputs.format_validity: Must match the entity/authorised person and be valid at signing; credentials, PINs and OTPs remain secret.

required_inputs.name: Active IEC and CBIC transmission status
required_inputs.when_required: ICEGATE, AD code, Customs and eBRC workflows
required_inputs.format_validity: Active ten-character IEC; current details confirmed and CBIC transmission checked.

required_inputs.name: Buyer/consignee identity and signed purchase order or sales contract
required_inputs.when_required: Commercial approval, logistics, bank and Customs documents
required_inputs.format_validity: Signed/current for the shipment; must state parties, goods, quantity, value, currency, delivery and document terms.

required_inputs.name: Payment instrument, payer, currency, due date and bank-routing instructions
required_inputs.when_required: Before accepting funds or dispatching documents
required_inputs.format_validity: Written and transaction-specific; LC/collection/third-party/direct-dispatch terms require bank confirmation.

required_inputs.name: Complete product technical and commercial dossier
required_inputs.issuer_or_provider: Manufacturer/exporter and test/regulatory issuers where applicable
required_inputs.when_required: Before classification, policy, licence, GST and shipping-bill decisions
required_inputs.format_validity: Model-specific, versioned, and complete for composition, function, process, end use, packaging, quantity and value.

required_inputs.name: SCOMET technical, software/technology, end-use and end-user dossier
required_inputs.issuer_or_provider: Manufacturer/exporter, buyer/end user and competent technical issuers
required_inputs.when_required: When a current SCOMET screen is positive or unresolved
required_inputs.format_validity: Exact technical parameters, model/software/technology scope, purchase order, destination, consignee, end user and end use; versioned to the application.

required_inputs.name: Shipment-specific ITC(HS), export-policy, regulator and export-duty memo
required_inputs.issuer_or_provider: Exporter/qualified customs adviser using current official sources
required_inputs.when_required: Before restricted/SCOMET route, GST route, logistics and Customs filing
required_inputs.format_validity: Tied to exact product facts and verification date; unresolved alternatives must be explicit.

required_inputs.name: Destination-country import and buyer-document requirement pack
required_inputs.issuer_or_provider: Foreign authority/importer or competent destination-country professional
required_inputs.when_required: Before final booking, production/labels and dispatch
required_inputs.format_validity: Country-, product-, importer- and date-specific; public/official evidence preferred and private advice identified.

required_inputs.name: GSTIN, registration status, tax route and return context
required_inputs.when_required: GST route, LUT, invoice, eBRC and refund
required_inputs.format_validity: Current registration and tax-period data; route must match the shipping bill and returns.

required_inputs.name: FORM GST RFD-11 LUT ARN
required_inputs.when_required: Before export without payment of IGST under LUT
required_inputs.format_validity: Applicable to the relevant period and exporter; ARN acknowledgement retained.

required_inputs.name: AD-bank branch code/account proof for customs registration
required_inputs.format_validity: Must identify the designated account/branch and match the ICEGATE entry; exact live upload format applies.

required_inputs.name: Approved shipping-bill and logistics data sheet
required_inputs.when_required: Booking, document preparation, shipping-bill filing and Customs presentation
required_inputs.format_validity: One controlled version consistent with contract, classification memo, GST route, licences and bank instructions.

required_inputs.name: Commercial invoice-cum-packing list, transport and regulatory support pack
required_inputs.when_required: Customs filing/presentation, carrier, bank and GST refund
required_inputs.format_validity: Final signed/version-controlled set; at minimum use the applicable FTP 2.06 documents plus product-specific documents.

required_inputs.name: Bank credit advice and Inward Remittance Message data
required_inputs.when_required: Payment receipt, AD document matching, reconciliation and eBRC
required_inputs.format_validity: Must match payer, purpose, currency, amount, date, account and order; corrections come from the bank.

required_inputs.name: Final invoice, shipping bill, LEO, transport/EGM and bank collection/matching set
required_inputs.issuer_or_provider: Exporter, Customs, carrier and AD bank
required_inputs.when_required: AD-bank lodgement, reconciliation, eBRC and non-realisation handling
required_inputs.format_validity: Final shipment identifiers and values; retain bank lodgement/export-bill reference.

required_inputs.name: GST returns, ledger, Statement 3/3A, invoice, shipping-bill, EGM and eligibility records
required_inputs.when_required: Only for an eligible accumulated-ITC refund claim
required_inputs.format_validity: Tax-period-specific and consistent across GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, invoice, shipping bill and EGM.

required_inputs.name: Overdue recovery, buyer dispute, extension/write-off, insurer and incentive/refund evidence
required_inputs.issuer_or_provider: Exporter, buyer, AD bank, courts/authorities or insurer as applicable
required_inputs.when_required: When proceeds are overdue, short or unrecoverable
required_inputs.format_validity: Contemporaneous and sufficient for the exact delegated/RBI/write-off/refund consequence invoked.

completion_proofs.name: Active IEC certificate and CBIC transmission status
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: IEC certificate/number, active profile and CBIC transmission indicator
completion_proofs.validation_method: Check DGFT IEC profile/View Any IEC and the logged-in CBIC transmission status against PAN/entity.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Foundation for Customs, bank, RCMC and eBRC records.

completion_proofs.name: ICEGATE registration confirmation
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: ICEGATE ID and successful login/registration acknowledgement
completion_proofs.validation_method: Use ICEGATE registration enquiry or authenticated profile and registered email acknowledgement.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Customs account, filing, AD-code, downloads and tracking.

completion_proofs.name: AD-bank export handling confirmation
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Written bank instruction/case with account, branch AD code, payment and document-routing route
completion_proofs.validation_method: Confirm with the bank's trade-finance/forex operations using the case reference.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Payment, Customs AD-code, EDPMS and exception handling.

completion_proofs.name: Signed order and export risk approval
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Signed PO/sales contract plus buyer/payment/document-risk checklist
completion_proofs.validation_method: Check signatures, buyer evidence, bank acceptance and internal approval against the shipment.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Commercial, bank, Customs and dispute evidence.

completion_proofs.name: Shipment-specific classification and policy memo
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Eight-digit ITC(HS), policy, conditions, regulator and export-duty decision with sources/date
completion_proofs.validation_method: Reperform against complete product facts and current DGFT/Customs sources; unresolved alternatives stop use.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Licence, GST, invoice, shipping bill and audit trail.

completion_proofs.name: Foreign import-requirements closure pack
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Foreign official/professional evidence and buyer/importer responsibility confirmation
completion_proofs.validation_method: Verify issuer, destination, product, importer, date and cited foreign authority; outside this pack's substantive validation.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Foreign clearance, contract and dispute prevention.

completion_proofs.name: Valid DGFT export authorisation
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Authorisation number/document and condition checklist
completion_proofs.validation_method: Check item, exporter, buyer/end user, quantity/value, validity, port and all conditions in the DGFT record.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Shipping-bill declaration and compliance proof.

completion_proofs.name: Valid SCOMET/competent-authority export permission
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Issued authorisation number/document, application record and condition checklist
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match exact category/item/technical scope, exporter, buyer/end user, destination, quantity/value, validity and every pre/post-export condition in the competent record.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Customs declaration, export-control audit and post-reporting.

completion_proofs.name: Current RCMC/equivalent certificate
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: e-RCMC/certificate number, issuer, product scope and validity
completion_proofs.validation_method: Check DGFT/issuer record and match the dependent authorisation/benefit.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Conditional FTP authorisation or benefit evidence.

completion_proofs.name: Approved GST export-route memo
