completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: GSTIN/status, LUT/bond/IGST route, export-duty and refund-eligibility caveat
completion_proofs.validation_method: Verify against current section 16, taxpayer facts and current notification/rule analysis.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Invoice, shipping bill, returns and refund audit trail.

completion_proofs.name: GST LUT ARN acknowledgement
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: FORM GST RFD-11 acknowledgement with ARN
completion_proofs.validation_method: Validate in the GST taxpayer account for the relevant period and exporter.
completion_proofs.retention_use: No-IGST export and possible refund support.

completion_proofs.name: Rule 96A LUT timing cure or relief
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Authenticated physical-export evidence, Commissioner-allowed further period, or tax-and-interest payment/return reference
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match invoice date, physical-export date, allowed period and exact tax/interest treatment to the GST record.
completion_proofs.retention_use: LUT compliance, refund review and audit.

completion_proofs.name: ICEGATE AD-code account registration success
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Foreign Remittance Account entry/status for exact customs location
completion_proofs.validation_method: Check authenticated Bank Account management against bank proof, AD code, account and location.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Shipping bill, remittance linkage and eligible refund/incentive routing.

completion_proofs.name: Approved shipment document pack
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Final invoice-cum-packing list, shipping data, licences/NOCs and carrier/bank/foreign checklist
completion_proofs.validation_method: Four-way consistency review across contract, invoice/packing, shipping-bill draft and bank instructions.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Customs, carrier, bank, buyer and audit file.

completion_proofs.name: Bank-reported inward remittance
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Credit advice and IRM number/data with account credit
completion_proofs.validation_method: Confirm payer, amount, currency, purpose, date and order reference with AD-bank trade operations.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Advance compliance, EDPMS reconciliation and eBRC.

completion_proofs.name: Customs-acknowledged shipping bill
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Shipping-bill acknowledgement, number/date and signed copy
completion_proofs.validation_method: Validate through ICEGATE/ICES and compare material fields to the approved document pack.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Customs, bank, GST, eBRC and buyer records.

completion_proofs.name: Resolved Shipping Bill acknowledgement/query state
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Positive CHCAE02_ACK/current accepted status, query reply and accepted amendment where applicable
completion_proofs.validation_method: Verify message IDs/status against the Shipping Bill number/date/location and confirm no material query remains open.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Permit Customs processing and preserve the filing audit trail.

completion_proofs.name: Let Export Order
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Signed LEO copy and gate pass where applicable
completion_proofs.validation_method: Download from ICEGATE e-Copy and match job/location/shipping bill.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Proof of Customs permission before loading.

completion_proofs.name: Transport document and EGM/physical-export confirmation
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Final AWB/BL/transport receipt plus shipping-bill-wise EGM or Customs status
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match carrier departure/transport identifiers to the shipping bill and verify EGM/physical-export status with Customs/ICEGATE.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Physical export, bank, GST refund and buyer evidence.

completion_proofs.name: AD-bank export-document lodgement reference
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Export-bill/document-lodgement reference and matching status
completion_proofs.validation_method: Confirm through bank trade-finance operations against shipping bill, invoice and IRM.
completion_proofs.retention_use: EDPMS, collection and realisation monitoring.

completion_proofs.name: AD-bank/EDPMS realisation reconciliation
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Matched export-bill/EDPMS status plus exporter reconciliation statement
completion_proofs.validation_method: Reconcile invoice, shipping bill, IRM, deductions and bank closure/matching reference.
completion_proofs.retention_use: FEMA completion and eBRC generation.

completion_proofs.name: Corrected Shipping Bill/EDPMS/DGFT transmission and matching record
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Final ICEGATE EDPMS status, rectification/retransmission result and AD-bank matched export entry
completion_proofs.validation_method: Compare Customs transmission, DGFT visibility, Shipping Bill, IRM and export-bill identifiers after correction.
completion_proofs.retention_use: FEMA monitoring and clean eBRC generation.

completion_proofs.name: Electronic Bank Realisation Certificate
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: eBRC number and downloadable certificate with clean status
completion_proofs.validation_method: Validate in DGFT Bills Repository and match IEC, IRM, AD code, shipping bill, currency, value and deductions; Under Review is not clean completion.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Documentary realisation proof for permitted tax/FTP/audit uses.

completion_proofs.name: Final clean eBRC remediation status
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Review disposition, permitted cancellation and replacement/final certificate with utilisation record
completion_proofs.validation_method: Check Bills Repository, IRM Utilisation Report and response/cancellation status; match final certificate to bank source data.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Documentary realisation proof and prevention of duplicate/invalid benefit use.

completion_proofs.name: GST refund disposition
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: RFD-01 ARN and final deficiency/sanction/rejection/payment order
completion_proofs.validation_method: Track in GST portal and reconcile credited amount/order with the eligible claim.
completion_proofs.retention_use: GST ledger, accounting and possible non-realisation consequence.

completion_proofs.name: Corrected GST refund or final rejection disposition
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: RFD-03/RFD-08/RFD-09, fresh ARN, RFD-06/RFD-05, bank validation and ledger re-credit records as applicable
completion_proofs.validation_method: Track the correct ARN/forms in the GST portal, verify bank/PFMS status and reconcile the final order/credit to the ledger.
completion_proofs.retention_use: GST accounting, appeal decision and refund audit trail.

completion_proofs.name: Approved non-realisation resolution
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Extension, recovery, EDPMS correction/closure/write-off and related GST/DGFT evidence
completion_proofs.validation_method: Check authority, conditions, period, EDPMS reporting, incentive surrender and refund consequences for the exact bill.
completion_proofs.retention_use: FEMA, GST, FTP, insurer and audit defence.

claims.statement: An IEC is mandatory for export/import activities and no goods export may be made without it unless specifically exempted.
claims.subject: IEC eligibility
claims.applicability: Commercial goods exporter not within a specific exemption.
claims.locator: FTP Chapter 2, paragraph 2.05 and 2.05(a)

claims.statement: The current DGFT IEC flow is online and requires the portal application, prescribed identity/address/bank inputs, supported signing, payment, certificate download, and CBIC transmission check.
claims.subject: IEC portal journey
claims.applicability: New IEC applicant.
claims.locator: IEC Module User Help File V4.1, section 5, pages 8-18, especially steps 1-10 and Screen 23 notes

claims.statement: The DGFT IEC manual states a new IEC application fee of INR 500 through the payment gateway.
claims.subject: IEC fee
claims.applicability: New IEC application; amount must be rechecked in the live payment step.
claims.locator: IEC Module User Help File V4.1, section 5 step 10, page 17

claims.statement: The ordinary mandatory export documents are the applicable transport receipt, commercial invoice-cum-packing list, and shipping bill/bill of export/postal bill, with additional documents possible for regulated goods.
claims.subject: Export document baseline
claims.applicability: Goods exported from India; mode and product-specific additions apply.
claims.locator: FTP Chapter 2, paragraph 2.06(a)-(d)

claims.statement: Goods may be exported without restriction except where regulated by ITC(HS), FTP, or another law in force.
claims.subject: Export policy default
claims.applicability: Subject to exact classification, later notifications, policy conditions, and other law.
claims.locator: FTP 2023, paragraph 2.40 Free Exports

claims.statement: DGFT Notification 50/2024-25 notified the harmonised Schedule II Export Policy for all ITC(HS) 2022 codes with item-specific policy conditions and updated general notes.
claims.subject: ITC(HS) Schedule II
claims.applicability: All chapters, subject to later item-specific amendments and current general notes.
claims.locator: Notification 50/2024-25 dated 13 January 2025, paragraphs 1-4

claims.statement: The exact ITC(HS), export-policy status, export duty, regulator conditions, SCOMET result, and authorisation path for a user shipment cannot be established until its complete product and transaction facts are classified against all current sources.
claims.subject: Shipment classification result
claims.applicability: Every case-specific product decision.
claims.locator: Framework only: FTP 2.06(c)-(d), 2.40, current Schedule II and Appendix 3; no case dossier supplied

claims.statement: Applications for restricted import/export goods are made online on the DGFT portal, and HBP identifies ANF 2N for non-SCOMET restricted export authorisation with prescribed documents.
claims.subject: Restricted export authorisation
claims.applicability: Non-SCOMET goods classified as Restricted; item-specific conditions control.
claims.locator: HBP Chapter 2, paragraphs 2.03(a) and 2.68

claims.statement: DGFT Notification 31/2025-26 revised Appendix 3, the SCOMET list under Schedule II, and the revised list came into force thirty days after 23 September 2025.
claims.subject: Current SCOMET control list
claims.applicability: Screening goods, software or technology potentially within SCOMET; later amendments still control.
claims.locator: Notification 31/2025-26 dated 23 September 2025, paragraphs 1-3, effect statement and revised Appendix 3

claims.statement: DGFT's SCOMET portal states that SCOMET export requires an issued authorisation and routes an ordinary fresh application through Export Management System to ANF 2O(A); GAICT uses the distinct ANF 2O(B) route.
claims.subject: SCOMET authorisation portal
claims.applicability: Ordinary DGFT-controlled SCOMET application; Category 0 and other competent-authority cases differ.
claims.locator: SCOMET User Help File v4.0, landing page and Apply for Export Authorisation of SCOMET Items, ANF 2O(A); GAICT section ANF 2O(B)

claims.statement: This pack does not determine whether the user's item, software or technology is SCOMET-controlled or whether DGFT/another competent authority would approve export because the technical, end-use, end-user and destination dossier is absent.
claims.subject: Case-specific SCOMET result
claims.applicability: Any positive or unresolved SCOMET screen.
claims.locator: Current list and portal framework only; no shipment-specific technical/end-use/end-user dossier

claims.statement: RCMC is required for an FTP authorisation other than the stated restricted-item exception or for another FTP benefit/concession, subject to specified exemptions and procedures.
claims.subject: RCMC applicability
claims.applicability: Only when the dependent FTP authorisation/benefit/concession triggers it.
claims.locator: FTP Chapter 2 paragraph 2.57(a); e-RCMC Customer Portal User Help File V4.0, prerequisites and Apply for e-RCMC, page 8

claims.statement: ECGC export-credit cover may protect against specified buyer insolvency/default and political risks, but protection depends on an issued cover.
claims.subject: Export credit insurance
claims.applicability: Exporter elects and obtains policy-specific cover for the buyer/country/terms.
claims.locator: FTP Chapter 2, paragraph 2.55(i)-(ii)

claims.statement: Export of goods is a zero-rated supply under section 16 of the IGST Act.
claims.subject: GST zero rating
claims.applicability: Supply qualifies as export of goods.
claims.locator: IGST Act section 16(1)(a)

claims.statement: A registered person making zero-rated supply may claim refund of unutilised ITC without payment of IGST under bond or LUT, subject to section 54 and prescribed conditions.
claims.subject: GST LUT/bond route
claims.applicability: Registered exporter satisfying the prescribed route and refund conditions.
claims.locator: IGST Act section 16(3)

claims.statement: Payment-of-IGST refund is limited to Government-notified classes of persons or goods/services, and export-duty goods are excluded from both unutilised-ITC and IGST-paid export refunds.
claims.subject: GST payment-of-tax route limitations
claims.applicability: Any proposed export-on-payment-of-IGST refund or export-duty goods.
claims.locator: IGST Act section 16(4)-(5)

claims.statement: A registered exporter submits FORM GST RFD-11 on the common portal and LUT is deemed accepted when the online acknowledgement bearing ARN is generated; no physical document is needed for acceptance.
claims.subject: GST LUT portal
claims.applicability: Exporter eligible to furnish LUT rather than bond.
claims.locator: Circular 40/14/2018-GST, paragraph 2(c)-(e)

claims.statement: Under Rule 96A, goods exported without IGST under bond/LUT must leave India within three months from invoice date or a Commissioner-allowed further period; otherwise the exporter binds itself to pay tax due with section 50(1) interest within fifteen days after expiry, and failure can withdraw the export facility and trigger recovery.
claims.subject: LUT goods-export timing and cure
claims.applicability: Registered person supplies goods for export without payment of IGST under bond/LUT.
claims.locator: CGST Rules, Rule 96A(1)(a), (2) and (3)

claims.statement: The GST portal route for accumulated-ITC refund on exports without tax uses FORM GST RFD-01, shipping-bill and EGM details, required returns, and ARN tracking.
claims.subject: GST refund portal procedure
claims.applicability: Exporter independently establishes refund eligibility for the relevant period.
claims.locator: GST portal user guide FAQ 1, steps 1-8

claims.statement: A refund deficiency is communicated electronically in RFD-03 and requires a rectified fresh application; a proposed whole/part rejection is issued in RFD-08, answered in RFD-09 within fifteen days, and decided through RFD-06 after opportunity of hearing.
claims.subject: GST refund deficiency and rejection response
claims.applicability: GST RFD-01 refund application receives a formal deficiency or proposed rejection.
claims.locator: Refund Rules, acknowledgement/deficiency and order provisions; Circular 125/44/2019-GST paragraphs 4-5 and electronic-processing discussion

claims.statement: GST's official refund advisory requires correction of failed refund bank-account validation through the permitted registration-bank amendment and ARN-linked Update Bank Account function, with status tracked on the dashboard/PFMS flow.
claims.subject: GST refund bank validation
claims.applicability: PFMS/GST bank validation fails for an RFD-01/RFD-05 refund flow.
claims.locator: Advisory on Refund Tracking, process diagram and bank-account validation/update instructions

claims.statement: This pack does not establish the exporter's shipment-specific GST refund entitlement or amount because registration, ITC, returns, export duty, notification class, values, and tax-period facts are not supplied.
claims.subject: GST refund entitlement
claims.applicability: Any proposed refund for the user shipment.
claims.locator: Framework only: IGST Act section 16(3)-(5) and GST portal eligibility/data checks; no taxpayer ledger/return facts supplied

claims.statement: A registered exporter that received unutilised-ITC refund for goods export is liable to deposit the refund with applicable interest within thirty days after the FEMA realisation period expires if sale proceeds are not realised, subject to prescribed treatment.
claims.subject: GST non-realisation consequence
claims.applicability: Refund received under IGST Act section 16(3) for export goods and proceeds not realised within FEMA period.
claims.locator: IGST Act section 16(3), proviso

claims.statement: ICEGATE registration is the prerequisite for online customs-document filing and provides an ICEGATE ID, tracking and electronic acknowledgements; Importer/Exporter is an eligible role.
claims.subject: ICEGATE registration
claims.applicability: Exporter uses ICEGATE direct/post-login services; broker/Service Centre channel may file on its behalf.
claims.locator: Registration FAQ v1.01 questions 1-9 and current Registration index listing Registration on ICEGATE dated 05-Jun-2025

claims.statement: ICEGATE Bank Account management supports adding a Foreign Remittance Account using bank, branch, AD code, account number, customs location, document type/IRN and proof.
claims.subject: AD-code registration
claims.applicability: IEC holder registers the designated AD bank account for the intended customs location.
claims.locator: AD Code Bank Account Registration Advisory, Add New Bank Account steps 1-6; live advisory page dated 25 August 2026

claims.statement: ICEGATE identifies CACHE01 Shipping Bill, CHCAE02_ACK positive acknowledgement, CHCAE02_NAK negative acknowledgement, CHCAE03 query and CACHE04 query-reply flows, and the current export message specification defines their filing structure.
claims.subject: Electronic Shipping Bill filing and rejection messages
claims.applicability: Supported exporter/customs-broker electronic filing channel.
claims.locator: ICEGATE e-Filing Messages rows 8-12 dated 8 May 2026; ICES export message format v3.3 List of Messages and Shipping Bill specification

claims.statement: ICEGATE's current enquiry route lets users check a Shipping Bill's details and current/EGM status using the Shipping Bill number, date and location, with post-login Enquiries for authenticated records.
claims.subject: Shipping Bill status enquiry
claims.applicability: A Shipping Bill number/date/location exists.
claims.locator: Current ICEGATE FAQ, Services > Quick Information/Public Enquiries or Services Widget > Enquiries; Shipping Bill enquiry fields and displayed current/EGM status

claims.statement: ICEGATE provides public Shipping Bill EDPMS status and authenticated Rectification of SB EDPMS Status/foreign-exchange-realisation details, allowing a user to raise a Customs-side rectification query.
claims.subject: Shipping Bill EDPMS status and rectification
claims.applicability: Shipping Bill transmission/status appears missing or incorrect; bank-side reporting remains with the AD bank.
claims.locator: SB EDPMS Advisory overview and steps; Public Enquiries Manual v1.01 section 5.3, pages 9-10

claims.statement: When a Shipping Bill is not visible at DGFT, ICEGATE provides a post-login DGFT Retransmission Facility using Shipping Bill date/number, port code and IEC, followed by a DGFT Retransmission Status enquiry.
claims.subject: Shipping Bill retransmission to DGFT
claims.applicability: Existing Shipping Bill is missing from DGFT visibility; the route does not establish benefit eligibility.
claims.locator: DGFT Re-Transmission User Manual v0.2, overview, sections 2-3, pages 3-12

claims.statement: Electronically filed shipping bills undergo Customs risk processing that may require assessment/examination or facilitation, and the proper officer issues LEO only after applicable checks.
claims.subject: Customs export clearance
claims.applicability: Ordinary ICES export shipment; exact risk outcome is case-specific.
claims.locator: Customs Manual 2025, Chapter 2 export-clearance discussion including paragraphs 8.6 and 17, and RMS/LEO sequence

claims.statement: Shipping lines/agents furnish shipping-bill-wise EGM electronically before departure, and the EGM transfer confirms physical export in the Customs EDI system.
claims.subject: Export General Manifest
claims.applicability: Carrier/shipping-line/agent manifest route; mode-specific equivalent handling must be confirmed.
claims.locator: Customs Manual 2025, Chapter 2 paragraphs 25.3 and 26.1

claims.statement: ICEGATE Download e-Copy lets an authorised user retrieve LEO acknowledgement and signed copy by date or job number.
claims.subject: LEO proof download
claims.applicability: Logged-in user with access to the issued export job.
claims.locator: Download Utility v1.08, sections 2.2, 2.2.1 and 2.2.2, pages 10-13

claims.statement: Export contracts and invoices may be denominated in freely convertible currency or Indian rupees, while the permitted manner of realisation depends on the applicable RBI/FTP route.
claims.subject: Export contract currency
claims.applicability: Ordinary export contract; special INR/ACU/SRVA routes require their conditions.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, A.1(v), including FTP paragraph 2.52 summary

claims.statement: The full export value is to be received through an AD bank in the manner specified by the applicable receipt-and-payment regulations.
claims.subject: Manner of export receipt
claims.applicability: Goods export proceeds unless a specific permitted route applies.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, A.3(i)

claims.statement: Third-party export payment is permitted only within RBI conditions: an irrevocable order backed by tripartite agreement or accepted substitute evidence, AD-bank bona-fides/export-document review, banking-channel payment, payer declaration in the export form and continued exporter responsibility for realisation/repatriation.
claims.subject: Third-party export payment
claims.applicability: Payer differs from the overseas buyer/contracting party.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, A.3(v) and B.8

claims.statement: The ordinary period to realise and repatriate full export proceeds is nine months from date of export.
claims.subject: FEMA realisation period
claims.applicability: Ordinary exporter; warehouse-abroad and special periods are excluded.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, A.2(i)

claims.statement: For ordinary advance receipt, shipment must be made within three years and shipment documents routed through the same AD bank through which the advance was received.
claims.subject: Advance against exports
claims.applicability: Ordinary export advance under C.2(1); special long-term arrangements differ.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, C.2(1), as updated through 17 July 2026

claims.statement: Exporters ordinarily lodge prescribed export/shipping documents with the named AD bank within twenty-one days; for EDI cases no EC copy is required where it is not printed and shipping-bill data is integrated with EDPMS.
claims.subject: AD-bank document lodgement
claims.applicability: Goods export through Customs port/EDI port; exact bank document set applies.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, B.1(iv)-(v) and B.2(i)-(iii)

claims.statement: For collection/LC handling, RBI allows HAWB/FCR documents only within stated AD-bank conditions, advises buyer due diligence, permits late document handling when the AD bank is satisfied with reasons, and limits direct dispatch to specified advance/LC/regular-customer cases.
claims.subject: AD-bank document-routing branches
claims.applicability: Exporter uses collection, LC, HAWB/FCR, late lodgement or direct dispatch; the selected bank's checklist still applies.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, B.11, C.7 and C.10

claims.statement: Direct dispatch of shipping documents is not a universal open-account right; it is permitted for full advance/full irrevocable LC with contract support or where the AD bank accepts the request based on customer standing and realisation arrangements.
claims.subject: Shipping-document dispatch
claims.applicability: Exporter proposes direct dispatch rather than normal AD-bank handling.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, C.10(i)-(iii)

claims.statement: RBI's export-document guidance advises exporters to ensure due diligence on the overseas buyer where forwarder cargo receipts or similar collection risks are used.
claims.subject: Buyer due diligence
claims.applicability: Commercial risk assessment; public sources do not prove a particular buyer is sound.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, B.11(ii)(b), concluding advice

claims.statement: AD banks report export transactions/receipts in EDPMS, maintain aligned export-bill records, update realised proceeds on an as-realised basis and generate bank-side eBRC only from EDPMS data.
claims.subject: EDPMS reporting
claims.applicability: Goods export handled by AD Category-I bank.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, B.1(v), C.14-C.15 and C.30

claims.statement: For an EDPMS entry/bill of INR 10 lakh equivalent or less, the AD bank must use the special reconciliation procedure based on the exporter's realisation declaration, may accept declared value reduction on that basis, and must not levy a penal charge for regulatory delay.
claims.subject: Small-value EDPMS reconciliation
claims.applicability: Individual EDPMS entry/bill is INR 10 lakh equivalent or less; bank still performs reconciliation/closure.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, C.31(i)-(ii)

claims.statement: AD banks must closely follow overdue export bills and report failure to realise or seek extension to the RBI Regional Office.
claims.subject: Overdue export bills
claims.applicability: Bill remains outstanding beyond due date/applicable period.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, C.15(i)-(iv)

claims.statement: AD Category-I banks may extend the realisation period up to six months at a time when C.20 conditions are met; other cases require RBI Regional Office approval and EDPMS reporting.
claims.subject: Extension of realisation period
claims.applicability: Exporter requests extension and satisfies the delegated conditions.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, C.20(i)-(iii)

claims.statement: Unrealised export bills may be self-written off or written off by the handling AD bank only within the current limits, categories, conditions, documentary evidence, incentive-surrender and EDPMS reporting rules; uncovered requests go to RBI.
claims.subject: Write-off of unrealised export bills
claims.applicability: Recovery failed and the exact C.23 conditions are established.
claims.locator: RBI Master Direction, C.23.1-C.23.10

claims.statement: DGFT's current eBRC process allows an IEC-linked exporter to generate eBRC on self-certification from bank-supplied IRM metadata through Services > eBRC > Generate e-BRC.
claims.subject: eBRC generation
claims.applicability: Supported IRM and goods shipment/invoice data exist.
claims.locator: eBRC User Guide for Exporters v1.2, introduction and section 6, pages 3 and 7-18

claims.statement: DGFT does not allow eBRC generation for an advance before the corresponding shipping-bill/invoice date, and the goods form requires AD code and shipping-bill data.
claims.subject: Advance eBRC linkage
claims.applicability: Advance inward remittance for a goods export.
claims.locator: eBRC User Guide v1.2, general guideline D pages 4 and 11; goods fields pages 12-15

claims.statement: An eBRC flagged by DGFT risk management shows Under Review, its IRM cannot be used, and the exporter responds through Services > eBRC > Respond to Bank/Agency with remarks/attachment until disposition.
claims.subject: eBRC exception handling
claims.applicability: DGFT RMS flags the eBRC/IRM.
claims.locator: eBRC User Guide v1.2, section 9 Risk Management System, pages 28-30

claims.statement: DGFT permits portal cancellation only for an exporter-generated self-certified eBRC that has not been used for benefits, incentives, IGST/refunds, remission or credits; bank-generated eBRC cannot use this cancellation route, and remarks, declaration and signature are mandatory.
claims.subject: eBRC cancellation
claims.applicability: Exporter-generated eBRC is incorrect and unused; utilised or bank-generated records require another competent route.
claims.locator: eBRC User Guide v1.2, section 7 Cancelling eBRC, pages 21-25

claims.statement: DGFT provides Bills Repository status and an IRM Utilisation Report whose request/report status can be Submitted, Processed or Failed, supporting a check of utilisation before correction or cancellation.
claims.subject: eBRC/IRM utilisation tracking
claims.applicability: Exporter verifies IRM/eBRC use or prepares remediation.
claims.locator: eBRC User Guide v1.2, repository fields pages 20-21 and section 8 IRM Utilisation Report pages 25-27

claims.statement: Failure to realise proceeds within the RBI period can require return of FTP benefits/incentives and action under foreign-trade law.
claims.subject: FTP non-realisation consequence
claims.applicability: Exporter availed FTP benefit/incentive against the unrealised export.
claims.locator: FTP Chapter 2, paragraph 2.54(a)-(c)

claims.statement: The destination-country import, product, labelling, sanctions, tax, origin, and importer requirements for the user shipment are not established by this India-Central pack.
claims.subject: Foreign import requirements
claims.applicability: Every shipment; exact foreign evidence depends on country, product and importer.
claims.locator: No foreign jurisdiction/product/importer was researched; external dependency by scope

claims.statement: Bank, correspondent, LC/collection, insurance, customs-broker, freight and handling charges are case-specific and no current shipment quote was supplied.
claims.subject: Private charges
claims.applicability: Selected service provider, route, instrument and shipment.
claims.locator: No provider tariff or quote supplied

demo_scenario.title: Bounded demo — first GST-registered micro exporter, simple goods, full advance
demo_scenario.purpose: Demonstrate an end-to-end first-order path that reaches physical export, AD-bank/EDPMS reconciliation and eBRC without generalising product or foreign-law assumptions.
assumptions: An Indian sole proprietorship with active PAN, domestic bank account and GST registration applies for its first IEC and ICEGATE access.
The order is for one small batch of non-perishable, non-hazardous, non-electronic manufactured consumer goods; this description is not itself a tariff classification.

Before the demo path begins, a qualified customs adviser signs a shipment-specific memo confirming the exact eight-digit ITC(HS), current policy status Free, no export duty, and no product-specific Central licence/NOC/SCOMET trigger.

The foreign buyer/importer supplies written destination-country clearance requirements and confirms that no certificate of origin or preferential claim is required for this shipment; those foreign conclusions are not validated or generalised here.
The signed order is denominated in USD and requires 100 percent advance from the named buyer through the selected AD Category-I bank before shipment.
The GST route is export without payment of IGST under an accepted LUT; no GST refund, drawback, RoDTEP, RCMC, preferential origin or other benefit is claimed in the demo.
A licensed customs broker files an air-cargo shipping bill at the confirmed location, and all private charges are taken only from written quotes.
The advance IRM is matched after shipment to the shipping bill through the same AD bank, then the exporter generates eBRC after the shipping-bill/invoice date.

qualifier_answers.answer: Sole proprietorship; PAN/bank/GST documents available; IEC initially absent.
Complete model-specific technical dossier supplied to a qualified customs adviser.
Named foreign buyer/consignee and written foreign import-responsibility pack supplied externally.
Free with no unmet condition, based only on the signed case memo assumed for this demo.
Full advance from the named buyer in USD through the designated AD bank.
No FTP authorisation, benefit or concession claimed; RCMC stays off path.
Licensed customs broker, with exporter ICEGATE access for account and document services.
Buyer/importer states none required; no preference claimed; external assumption only.
No post-shipment receivable because full advance is required; no insurance reliance.

out_of_scope_facts: The actual eight-digit ITC(HS), duty, regulator and foreign requirements are not asserted by the generic goods description.
Foreign import clearance, taxes, labels, standards, sanctions and importer eligibility remain external evidence.
No GST refund, drawback, RoDTEP, RCMC, CoO, credit insurance or other benefit is claimed.
No SCOMET, restricted, prohibited, state-trading, specialist-goods, postal/courier, SEZ/EOU or consignment route is demonstrated.
No private actor fee, service time, Incoterm, or buyer-credit conclusion is generalised.
action_required_gates: Obtain and retain the actual product classification/policy/duty/regulator memo before using the happy path.
Obtain destination-country/importer evidence from a competent foreign source before booking/dispatch.
Obtain selected AD-bank written acceptance of the USD advance, purpose, AD code, shipment-document and EDPMS matching route.
Confirm active IEC/CBIC transmission, ICEGATE login, AD-code location status and LUT ARN in the live portals.
Reconcile the advance IRM and shipping bill after export and do not accept an Under Review or mismatched eBRC as completion.
demo_scenario.non_universality_note: This scenario is a bounded demonstration only. Changing the goods, destination, payer, currency, payment instrument, GST status, export-duty status, benefit claim, shipping mode/location, entity, or foreign requirements reopens the relevant qualifier and can change the graph.
